newsitem.title: GERMANY: OECD-Beware linking German monetary, fiscal policy.
newsitem.headline: OECD-Beware linking German monetary, fiscal policy.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) advised against closely linking German monetary policy to expectations about taxes and budget deficits.
In its annual country report on Germany, the OECD said while tighter fiscal policy should leave the Bundesbank more room for manoeuvre on interest rates, the fiscal outlook remains uncertain.
"As a result, any strategy linking the response of monetary policy directly to the announced orientation of fiscal policy would carry significant risk," the report said.
"Monetary policy thus needs to adopt a wait-and-see posture."

The Paris-based institution, which finished writing the report on July 26, before the Bundesbank cut the securities repurchase rate thirty basis points to three percent, said there was further room to ease monetary policy.
But at a press conference in Bonn on Thursday, the OECD's representative in Germany Dieter Menke called the repo cut "just such a step."
The OECD added that monetary measures already taken should help support the economy in the rest of the year.
